title: The genome in plain words, re-derived against the new brain
question: Do these fourteen sentences read like a description of an animal? And is LAYS NOTHING IT FOLLOWS clear enough that you'd know it was reporting a fault rather than describing a design?
context_md:
You asked, on 2 September: *"is the genome plain text accurate? is it that
simple like there is just a switch for drop food at the colony?"*

The answer then was yes — one weight, `AtNest -> Drop`. **The card I posted
that day is now describing a machine that does not exist**, so please judge
this one instead of it.

Since then the brain was rebuilt underneath this work: four new senses, a
twelfth verb, twice the hidden layer, and the way an ant finds its way home
moved out of the engine and into the genome. Re-deriving these sentences
against the new brain is what this card is.

**Two of the lines here are new because the animal changed:**

- `DUMPS SPOIL AT THE NEST` — putting down dug soil used to be the same gene
  as putting down food, so nothing could select for one against the other.
  They are two verbs now, and they needed two vocabularies.
- `LAYS NOTHING IT FOLLOWS` — and this one is a bug report.

**That last line is the part worth your attention.** Chasing why the old
`ALWAYS LAYS HOME SCENT` disappeared turned up a live fault: **no ant has
laid a home scent since 2 September.** Not a faint one — none, ever. The
setting that charges it is about twenty times too quiet for the engine to
hear at all, so it is mixed at zero. The food trail is unaffected. Both
species that have a homing sense have it, and they are the only two settings
in the whole tree that are below the engine's hearing.

I have **not** fixed it: turning the setting up twenty-fold changes how fast
the scent fades, and the two numbers either side of it were tuned against the
quiet value, so it needs re-tuning rather than a one-line change. It is
written up as a known fault (§Z5) with the measurement and a reproduction.

So the page is telling you the truth about an animal that is currently
missing half its way home — which is the thing a page like this is for.
